findings.title: Double-clicking a name to select it still toggles the row once
findings.body: The guard reads the selection when the click arrives, so it covers a drag-select. A double-click does not get the same treatment. Its first `click` comes before any selection exists, so it toggles the row. Chromium selects the word on the second mousedown, so only the second click is skipped. The row ends up flipped, which is the same side effect the earlier thread described, just reached by double-click (and triple-click) instead of drag. It does show on screen as a dimmed row and a changed summary. One option is to toggle only on `event.detail === 1` and undo the toggle when `event.detail === 2` and a selection exists. Another is to make only the non-text parts of the row (padding, icon, arrow) the toggle target. If double-click copying isn't a use case you care about, leave it as is.

contracts.action: A click on a selectable finding row is skipped when `window.getSelection()` has text
contracts.equivalent_path: The checkbox's own onChange (Check component), which calls setFixing directly and is not affected by the guard because clicks on the input return earlier
contracts.before_after: Before: any click on the row other than on the input called setFixing([path], !fixing). After: the same, unless the document has a non-empty selection when the click is dispatched. That covers a drag-select that starts and ends inside the row. A double-click's first click still toggles, because no selection exists yet.
contracts.visible_effect: When the toggle is skipped, the row keeps its state: no .rowOff dimming change, and the same summary and Fix button label. When it toggles, .rowOff dims the row and strikes through the new name.
contracts.failure_mode: window.getSelection() is synchronous and its result is optional-chained, so a null selection falls through to the toggle. No async path is involved.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed: line 216 returns before `setFixing` when there's a selection, so a drag-select no longer toggles the row, and the test pins it. One smaller case is still open: double-clicking to select a word toggles the row once, because the first click comes before the selection exists. I've noted it separately as a consider.
